skill.name: sbom-syft
skill.description: Generate Software Bills of Materials with Syft for container images, directories, and archives. Use the guidance for dependency visibility, vulnerability scanning, license review, CI artifacts, and signed SBOM attestations.
skill.summary: Generate and use Syft SBOMs for supply chain security workflows.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, reference links, or defensive security templates. The CI template contains a confirmed remote installer piped to bash and unpinned scanner installation guidance that should be hardened before publication.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash in the CI template.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl pipe-to-shell installation with a pinned release, checksum verification, or a maintained pinned GitHub Action.

remediation.issue: Security scanners are installed without pinned versions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions and action revisions for Semgrep, Safety, TruffleHog, Trivy, Checkov, tfsec, and related tools.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes placeholder credentials in Syft configuration examples.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that registry credentials must come from a secret manager or CI secret store, not committed configuration files.

content.value_statement: Teams need accurate SBOMs to track dependencies, vulnerabilities, and licenses. This skill guides Syft workflows for containers, filesystems, CI pipelines, and signed attestations.
actual_capabilities: Guides SBOM generation for container images, directories, archives, and release artifacts.
Explains CycloneDX, SPDX, syft-json, and human-readable Syft outputs.
Combines Syft SBOMs with Grype vulnerability scanning workflows.
Shows CI/CD artifact handling and security scan integration patterns.
Covers signed SBOM attestations with cosign.
limitations: Requires Syft or a compatible container image to be installed by the user.
Does not verify generated SBOM accuracy without reviewing source artifacts.
Template commands may need security hardening before direct use in CI.
Cannot replace legal review for license compliance decisions.

use_cases.title: Inventory Container Dependencies
use_cases.description: Generate CycloneDX or SPDX SBOMs for release images before deployment.

use_cases.title: Add SBOMs to Releases
use_cases.description: Attach SBOM artifacts and attestations to build outputs for provenance records.

use_cases.title: Review Dependency Licenses
use_cases.description: Use Syft output to identify package licenses and prepare compliance review inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Generate First SBOM
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me generate a CycloneDX SBOM for my container image using Syft. Ask for the image name if missing.

prompt_templates.title: Scan Project Directory
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through creating an SBOM for this project directory. Include format choice, exclusions, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add CI Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my CI pipeline and add SBOM generation with artifact upload. Pin tools and avoid remote shell installers.

prompt_templates.title: Design Provenance Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an SBOM and vulnerability management workflow for a multi-architecture container release. Include signing, verification, and evidence retention.

output_examples.input: Generate an SBOM for a production container image.
output_examples.output: A concise Syft workflow with target confirmation, output format selection, storage advice, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Compare SBOMs for two application releases.
output_examples.output: A dependency change summary covering added packages, removed packages, version changes, and review priorities.
A pipeline outline with scanner setup, artifact retention, vulnerability gating, and signing steps.

best_practices: Pin scanner versions and verify downloaded tools before running them in CI.
Store SBOMs with build metadata so each artifact maps to a release.
Restrict SBOM access when package names reveal private architecture.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote install scripts directly into a shell.
Do not treat generated SBOMs as complete without spot-checking package detection.
Do not publish SBOMs with internal package details unless disclosure is approved.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create SBOMs with Syft for containers, directories, archives, and release workflows.

faq.question: Which SBOM formats are covered?
faq.answer: It covers CycloneDX, SPDX, Syft native output, GitHub dependency submission, and text formats.

faq.question: Can it scan vulnerabilities directly?
faq.answer: It explains how to pair Syft SBOMs with Grype or similar vulnerability scanners.

faq.question: Does it require Docker?
faq.answer: Docker is useful for container workflows, but local Syft can scan images, archives, and directories.

faq.question: Can it support compliance audits?
faq.answer: It provides SBOM generation and retention guidance that can support audit evidence collection.

faq.question: What should I review before using templates?
faq.answer: Review tool installation commands, version pinning, credential handling, and artifact access controls.
